cardsfix.text:
Card pages, shared shape:
• Header: name, kind, version, status, one-line description; uid shortened with copy.
• Kind-specific hero: Agent = composition graph, Prompt = the messages, Model = interface + artifacts.
• Vitals only from real sources (Revision 15): invoke_agent spans and vala.gateway.calls with this card_uid; otherwise an empty state naming what fills it. Prompt has no vitals.
• Verification table: the Verifiers bound to it, with trend and latest.
• Right rail: relationships with kind pills, compact metadata.
• Tabs: Overview · Versions · YAML (raw).
Gone: one box per spec field, "Declared empty." boxes, full hashes, "read-only projection of server truth".

Revision 12: Data (schema + stats), Service (components with their own verification) and Verifier (pipeline + bindings) join Agent, Prompt and Model. The other kinds keep the generic page.

changesnote.text:
Change Request (proposal, not on main yet). Revision 15: pages follow the existing GitHub-like mock in features/changes; Override and Claims removed.
• A server-owned record, not a Card. Any update makes a new immutable revision.
• Subjects: one or more repo + base…head (+ PR). Many PRs and repos can belong to one CR; a PR opens a CR when none is linked.
• The repo's wyrd.toml names a folder of Verifier Cards and which are required. Their requirements are what the change must meet.
• A user or process submits inputs/evidence to a revision; Verifiers judge that evidence against their requirements. A Verifier whose inputs are missing shows 'waiting on evidence'.
• Anyone can request another Verifier on a revision.
• Results land in vala.verification.results, so Verify, Query and Card pages show them.
• Verifier definitions load from the default branch, never from the PR under review.

fix.text:
What changes, by your four points:
1. One aligned toolbar row: SQL bar (plain text = name/trace-id match), zoom −/+, reset, time picker, Live. The separate search box, SORT and duration rows go: sort lives in column headers, duration is a facet + SQL.
2. Time picker button opens presets (5m → 30d) with custom range inside it.
3. Zooming shows a 'Zoomed … ✕' chip and the ↺ button returns to the preset you came from.
4. The from/to row you saw is the absolute-range editor that appears after a zoom; it moves into the picker.
Revision 2: amber removed from charts (lime is the secondary series; amber stays only on the WARN label). Traces lead with three linked charts: spans/min, errors, duration p50/p95.

provenance.text:
Revision 15 rules (spec REQ-021–REQ-030):
• No invented data: every number is a query on a named table or a spec value; every chart has Open in Query; empty states name the attribute or binding that fills them.
• Services: new service_card_uid column on spans, logs, metrics and gateway calls, from resource attribute wyrd.service.card_uid (OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES), scope-checked; defaults from a credential bound to one Service. card_uid stays the producing component.
• Custom charts live in ServiceSpec.charts (sql or sql_file; $1/$2 range, $3 bucket; shape rules per type; validated at registration).
• Verifier pages follow VerifierSpec: one check per requirement, step-scoped and Verifier-level requirements, decide; mode inferred.
• Missing on main: service_card_uid, ServiceSpec.charts, Change Requests, listing in-flight executions.

querynote.text:
Query (extends foundation Q-01):
• Same toolbar row: time range applies to each table's time column; limit; Copy SQL; CSV; Run ⌘↵ / Cancel.
• Catalog of real vala tables; correlation columns (card_uid, run_id) highlighted — they join any table.
• Starter queries show the joins (spans ⋈ verification.results on run_id).
• Results: Table · Chart (line/bar/area/number, x/y/group from result columns) · Details (query id, status, time, rows, bytes, error) · History.
• card_uid values render as their Card.
• Bounds shown are Oracle's real ones: one read-only SELECT, SQL ≤ 64 KiB, 2 h default deadline; the page's Limit bounds rows.

shellnote.text:
Revision 12: left rail on every page, matching Shell.svelte in code.
• Order: Home · Cards | Observe · Verify · Query | Changes; Settings and the user are pinned to the bottom.
• ⌘K moves into the rail (find a Card, run a saved view, or ask for one).
• The top bar keeps only the breadcrumb and page-level controls (time picker, Live).
• Drift is no longer an Observe tab: drift is a Verifier requirement, so it lives in Verify.

tracenote.text:
Revision 14, the Traces page (observability only):
• Traces mode: one row per trace (its root span): start, name, service, duration, spans, errors, status. Agent runs add model/tool calls, tokens, cost. Counts load only for rows on screen.
• Spans mode: every matching span, flat and sortable. Same toolbar, time range and WHERE.
• Live: new traces arrive at the top; scrolling, hovering or opening a trace pauses it; '↑ N new' resumes. Running traces fill in place.
• Click a trace: a drawer opens over the list (not beside it) and loads only that trace. Waterfall collapsed below 2 levels with pinned parents; span details below with Messages for LLM spans. Esc closes; Expand makes it a page; the URL is shareable.
• Filters (Service, Status, Duration, http.route, Root span, + any field) are open by default and can be hidden; clicking a value writes it into WHERE, which is always the real filter.
• Revision 15: Service filter is service_card_uid; Card filter is card_uid.

verifynote.text:
Revision 18 (spec REQ-026/027): Verify is the one results list, shaped like Traces. A row opens a drawer over the list (Expand for a full page). One Verifier graph, built from the spec, is the Card's definition and, coloured by recorded outcomes, the result view. The Card has no Results tab.

The UI never decides pass or fail: it renders recorded results.

Open: non-sensitive per-requirement outcomes; group_by close rule; session vs member results sharing group_id; multi-feature drift pass rule.

Illustrative: the session-resolution Verifier and drift scores are invented; no fixture exists yet.
